atoms.name: Decoder
atoms.one_line: An $n$-to-$2^n$ decoder raises exactly one output (a minterm); bigger ones are trees of smaller ones.

atoms.name: Multiplexer basics
atoms.one_line: A $2^n$-to-1 mux has $n$ select lines and passes data input number $S$ to the output.

atoms.name: Functions with a multiplexer
atoms.one_line: Selects take $n-1$ variables; each data input is $0$, $1$, $x$ or $\bar x$ from a minterm pair.

atoms.name: Mux trees and cascades
atoms.one_line: Collapse each mux to a signal, then work backwards from the output mux.

atoms.name: Half and full adders
atoms.one_line: Half adder: $S=a\oplus b$, $C=ab$. Full adder: $S=a\oplus b\oplus c$, $C=ab+(a\oplus b)c$.

atoms.name: Ripple and look-ahead carry
atoms.one_line: Ripple delay grows as $n$; look-ahead uses $C_{i+1}=G_i+P_iC_i$ expanded, with $\Theta(\log n)$ depth for fan-in 2.

atoms.name: Circuit output as minterm sets
atoms.one_line: AND intersects, OR unions, XOR takes the symmetric difference, NOT complements the set.

atoms.name: Universal gates and gate counts
atoms.one_line: NAND or NOR alone builds everything; XOR needs four NANDs; count shared sub-terms.

atoms.name: Delay and hazards
atoms.one_line: Circuit delay is the longest path; unequal delays create glitches such as $X\bar X$ pulsing to 1.

atoms.name: Adder-subtractor and encoders
atoms.one_line: XOR on $B$ with $K=C_0$ gives $A\pm B$; a priority encoder reports the highest asserted input.
